verdict.rationale: Gecko is a code security scanner, so running it as a pre-commit hook is a fair question for this kind of product. However, the evidence shows no pre-commit hook, local CLI, or commit-time scanning. Its documented scanning happens after code reaches the repository: GitHub App repo scans, PR pass/fail checks, ZIP or URL uploads, and API-triggered scans. These are adjacent features that do not stop secrets or issues from entering git history.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the scanner as a pre-commit hook so secrets and issues never enter my git history
